summary.intent: Build a stacked set of three PRs (A: wire-compat docs, B: redaction fix for PYPI_TOKEN/NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN, C: add cause to E176 and report PyPI statuses as ProviderStatus) using failing-tests-first, as part of Wave 1.
summary.outcome: PRs A (#217) and B (#218) were opened with stacked bases and green `just ci`. PR C was implemented test-first (three PyPI status tests red then fixed, new E176 test green) and its `just ci` gate completed with exit code 0, but it had not yet been committed, pushed, or linked into the stack.

repo: Work happens in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/wave1-stack, with PRs stacked A -> B -> C using stacked bases.
`just ci` is the full gate run per PR and can run in the background while unrelated work (opening other PRs) proceeds.
Error codes such as E176 are documented in docs/errors.md and need a docs row update when behavior changes.
Each PR needs a changeset file under .changeset/.
Provider cause text lives in callisto-model's release_observation.rs and error types in callisto-graph's error.rs; the cause is threaded through two constructor sites in provider/mod.rs.
Registry (PyPI) status classification is in provider/registry.rs with tests in provider/registry/tests.rs.
workflow: Failing tests first: change existing tests to demand new behavior, confirm exactly the expected tests are red, then implement the fix.
Write PR bodies and helper scripts to a temp job directory and run them via Bash to keep commands simple.
Use waiting on background task notifications to read a gate's exit line and tree state before committing.

friction: A new test initially failed to compile due to a missing qualified path, requiring a rerun of the provider tests.
open_items: Commit and push PR C, then link A, B, and C as a native stack.
Wave 1 remaining items (W10a on walk.rs, W9a/W9b) are blocked until #214 merges.
